pull.title: KAFKA-20292: Avoid copying share group assignable partitions in GroupSpecBuilder
pull.body:
Pass the share group state partition metadata to ShareGroupSpecBuilder
and look up assignable partitions in a ShareGroupSpecImpl subclass,
instead of copying the initialized partitions into GroupSpecImpl on
every share group assignment, and again for assignor offload. The
metadata is unmodifiable, so no copy is needed.

With that copy gone, the group spec builders no longer copy anything for
assignor offload, so remove the assignorOffload flag from the consumer,
share and streams group spec builders. The tests that covered offload
now check that group specs are not affected by modifications made after
they are built.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reviewers: David Jacot <dajac@apache.org>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

review_comments.body: I wonder whether we should just remove `assignorOffload` now. Dead code looks weird.

We usually use this pattern when the top class is abstract. Calling new `GroupSpecImpl.ShareGroupSpecImpl()` feels a bit weird. How about putting `ShareGroupSpecImpl` in its own file and renaming `GroupSpecImpl` to `ConsumerGroupSpecImpl`?
We can remove it. I would keep the tests for group spec immutability since we really want that to not break for async assignors.
Moved `ShareGroupSpecImpl` out to its own file. Are you sure you want `GroupSpecImpl` renamed? I think it's odd for `ShareGroupSpecImpl` to inherit from `ConsumerGroupSpecImpl`.

Seing this, I wonder if we should have ConsumerGroupSpecImpl and move it into it. If we don't want to have topicPartitionAllowedMap in the GroupSpec, it would make sense to remove assignedTopicPartitions too. Have you considered it?

Hm, `ShareGroupSpecImpl.isPartitionAssigned` still needs an implementation and the natural way to do it is the same as for consumer groups. Unless we decide to throw a `NotSupportedException` in `isPartitionAssigned`?

I'm not opposed to defining a `ConsumerGroupSpecImpl` and common `GroupSpecImpl` base class to keep things organized. It's just that I can't see `ConsumerGroupSpecImpl` holding any extra logic right now.
Ah, right... My bad. I thought that it was not needed because it is not used. However, it could be used.

issue.title: KAFKA-21318, KAFKA-20292: Compute GroupSpecImpl's assigned partitions lazily

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
Replace GroupSpecImpl's inverted target assignment with a BitSet of the
assigned partitions of each topic, computed from the members' current
assignments on the first call to isPartitionAssigned. Only the uniform
homogeneous assignor calls isPartitionAssigned, so other assignors no
longer compute it.

This makes build in TargetAssignmentBuilderBenchmark ~40% faster for
homogeneous groups, because isPartitionAssigned no longer looks up
partitions in the inverted target assignment's TimelineHashMaps, which
are slower than regular maps.

It also fixes a bug where the assignor saw the partitions of members
removed in the same request as still assigned. The bug is not reachable
today, since we do not compute a new target assignment when a member
leaves, only on the next heartbeat, and static member replacement keeps
the replaced member's partitions assigned.

Remove ModernGroup's inverted target assignment, since it is no longer
read. For share groups, it was never correct, because a partition can be
assigned to several members of a share group, while the inverted target
assignment holds a single member per partition.

Rename buildAssignment in TargetAssignmentBuilderBenchmark to
buildGroupSpecAndAssignment, which builds a new group spec on every
invocation, so that the cost of computing the assigned partitions is
included, and replace buildGroupSpecWithoutOffload and
buildGroupSpecWithOffload with an assignorOffload parameter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reviewers: David Jacot <dajac@apache.org>

issue.title: KAFKA-21360: Revoke topics no member subscribes to in the heterogeneous share assignor

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
SimpleHeterogeneousAssignmentBuilder computes per-topic assignments only
for topics in the union of the members' subscriptions. As a result,
partitions of topics that no member subscribes to anymore were carried
over from the existing assignment into the new target assignment.

Revoke these topics before computing the per-topic assignments, matching
the homogeneous builder's behavior, and remove the unreachable branch in
revokeUnassignablePartitions that attempted to handle them.

Reviewers: Sean Quah <squah@confluent.io>
